argument_markdown:
## Setup and exact target

Let $M:=\mathcal{M}_{8,1}$ and $\overline{M}:=\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{8,1}$. Then
$$\dim M=d=3\cdot 8-3+1=22.$$
By RED-0001 and FND-0001, the unresolved open input for the degree-$16$ pure-Tate induction at this pair is the pure-weight Borel–Moore piece
$$W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M),$$
expected to be of Tate type $\mathbb{Q}(8)$. Poincaré duality realizes the same pure motive as
$$W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)\;\simeq\;W_{28}H^{28}(M)(22),$$
so the untwisted ordinary pure piece $W_{28}H^{28}(M)$ is expected of type $\mathbb{Q}(-14)$ (Chow codimension $14$).

Equivalently, in the cohomological form of the Arbarello–Cornalba / CLP boundary sequence, the open pure-weight quotient controlling $H^{16}(\overline{M})$ is
$$W_{16}H^{16}(M)\;=\;\mathrm{im}\bigl(H^{16}(\overline{M};\mathbb{Q})\to H^{16}(M;\mathbb{Q})\bigr),$$
a pure Hodge structure of weight $16$ (and a quotient of the pure weight-$16$ group $H^{16}(\overline{M})$). Hard Lefschetz on $\overline{M}$ identifies the pure-Tate question for $H^{16}(\overline{M})$ with that for $H^{28}(\overline{M})$; the open pure pieces $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ and $W_{28}H^{28}(M)$ are likewise dual (up to the Tate twist $(22)$) via Poincaré duality on the smooth stack $M$.

Thus a refutation of CONJ-0001 at $(g,n)=(8,1)$ would require a **non-Tate direct summand inside this exact pure piece** $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ (equivalently inside $W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)$), not merely non-Tate cohomology of $M$ in some other weight or degree.

## Known non-Tate cohomology of $M_{8,1}$ (wrong bidegree)

By CLPW24 / CLPW25b:

- $3g+2n=26\ge 25$, so $H^*(M)$ is **not** of Tate type;
- the weight-$11$ Euler characteristic vanishes, $\chi_{11}(M_{8,1})=0$;
- the weight-$13$ Euler characteristic does not: $\chi_{13}(M_{8,1})=-2$;
- more precisely, for $3g+2n\in\{26,27\}$,
  $$\mathrm{gr}^W_{13}H_c^{k(g,n)}(M_{g,n})\;\simeq\;Z_{g,n}\otimes \mathsf{LS}_{12},$$
  with $k(8,1)=3\cdot 8+1-2=23$ and $Z_{8,1}\simeq\mathbb{Q}$, hence
  $$\mathrm{gr}^W_{13}H_c^{23}(M_{8,1})\;\simeq\;\mathsf{LS}_{12}.$$

**Weight bookkeeping.** Poincaré duality on the smooth stack of complex dimension $22$ pairs
$$\mathrm{gr}^W_k H_c^i(M)\quad\text{with}\quad\mathrm{gr}^W_{44-k}H^{44-i}(M).$$
In particular $\mathrm{gr}^W_{13}H_c^{23}$ pairs with $\mathrm{gr}^W_{31}H^{21}$, **not** with $W_{16}H^{16}$ or $W_{28}H^{28}$.

Therefore the established non-Tate summand $\mathsf{LS}_{12}$ of $M_{8,1}$ lies in the wrong pure graded piece for the degree-$16$ induction. Non-polynomial point counts of $M_{8,1}$ (equivalently $\chi_{13}\ne 0$) do **not** produce a non-Tate summand in $W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)$.

## Candidate non-Tate motives and elimination by weight

Write $\mathsf{L}:=H^2(\mathbb{P}^1)\simeq\mathbb{Q}(-1)$ (weight $2$), $\mathsf{S}_{12}:=W_{11}H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,11})$ (weight $11$), $\mathsf{S}_{16}:=W_{15}H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,15})$ (weight $15$), and $\mathsf{LS}_{12}:=\mathsf{L}\otimes\mathsf{S}_{12}$ (weight $13$). The pure piece $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ is pure of weight $16$ and is a quotient of $H^{16}(\overline{M})$, hence any irreducible summand also appears in $H^{16}(\overline{M})$.

| Candidate | Weight | Can it embed in pure weight $16$? |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $11$ (odd) | No |
| $\mathsf{L}^a\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $11+2a$ (always odd) | No: $11+2a=16$ forces half-integral $a$ |
| $\mathsf{LS}_{12}$ | $13$ (odd) | No (and known occurrence is in $\mathrm{gr}_{13}H_c^{23}$) |
| $\mathsf{S}_{16}$ | $15$ (odd) | No |
| $\mathsf{L}^a\mathsf{S}_{16}$ | $15+2a$ (always odd) | No: $15+2a=16$ impossible |
| $\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $22$ | No: $22>16$ |
| $\mathsf{L}^a\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $22+2a\ge 22$ | No in weight $16$ |
| $\mathsf{S}_{12}\otimes\mathsf{S}_{12}$ | $22$ | No in weight $16$ |
| $\mathsf{S}_{12}\otimes\mathsf{S}_{16}$ | $26$ | No in weight $16$ |
| top-weight $\mathrm{gr}^W_0 H_c^*$ | $0$ (Tate) | Wrong weight; Tate type $\mathbb{Q}$ |
| $\mathsf{L}^8$ | $16$ | Tate: $\mathbb{Q}(-8)$ |

Under the Chenevier–Lannes classification of conductor-$1$ motives of weight $\le 22$ (Payne survey, Thm. 4.1 / CL19), the only effective irreducible of pure weight $16$ is a Tate twist of the unit motive. There is **no** non-Tate conductor-$1$ pure motive of weight $16$. Consequently any non-Tate summand in $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ would already contradict those arithmetic predictions (or would require conductor $>1$ / motives outside the expected list), and no geometric construction presently supplies such a summand on $\overline{M}_{8,1}$ or on $M_{8,1}$.

For the dual pure piece $W_{28}H^{28}(M)$ (weight $28$), non-Tate candidates such as $\mathsf{L}^3\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathsf{S}_{12}$ (weight $28$) become weight-legal, but:

1. $W_{28}H^{28}(M)=\mathrm{im}\bigl(H^{28}(\overline{M})\to H^{28}(M)\bigr)$ is again a subquotient of compactified cohomology;
2. hard Lefschetz identifies $H^{28}(\overline{M})\simeq H^{16}(\overline{M})$ up to powers of an ample tautological class, so a non-Tate summand in $H^{28}(\overline{M})$ is equivalent to one in $H^{16}(\overline{M})$;
3. $\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathsf{S}_{12}$ is first predicted only in weight $22$, outside the pure-Tate range $k\le 20$, and no published computation places $\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathsf{S}_{12}$ (or a Tate twist) in $H^{16}$ or $H^{28}$ of $\overline{M}_{8,1}$.

Thus no known non-Tate structure is available as a concrete summand of the **exact** open pure-weight input for degree $16$.

## Compactification induction and survival

From THM-0003, the boundary sequence is right exact
$$H_{14}(\widetilde{\partial\overline{M}})\longrightarrow H_{16}(\overline{M})\longrightarrow W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M)\longrightarrow 0$$
(cohomologically: $H^{14}(\widetilde{\partial})\to H^{16}(\overline{M})\to W_{16}H^{16}(M)\to 0$). A non-Tate summand of the open pure piece would inject (as a quotient summand) into $H^{16}(\overline{M})$ and survive the induction, refuting CONJ-0001 at $(8,1)$. Conversely, every class in $H^{16}(\overline{M})$ is built from boundary classes of lower genus/markings plus this open pure piece.

For $(8,1)$ the inequality of THM-0004 applies ($n=1$ and $k=16\ge 2g=16$), so this open pure piece is an essential base case: it is not killed a priori by virtual cohomological dimension or forgetful pullback. CKgP is not known in genus $8$ (THM-0005 stops at genus $\le 7$), so algebraicity of $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ is unavailable.

**Conclusion of the search.** Every published non-Tate motivic structure known to appear on $M_{8,1}$ (primarily $\mathsf{LS}_{12}$ in weight $13$) is excluded from $W_{16}H^{16}(M)$ by weight and degree. No construction of a non-Tate summand inside the exact Borel–Moore target $W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M_{8,1})$ is obtained. The search therefore yields **no refutation** of the degree-$16$ pure-Tate statement at $(8,1)$. Establishing Tate type (or producing a counterexample) for this base case remains open, consistent with OBS-0001.

## Gaps

- No complete computation of $W_{16}H^{16}(M_{8,1})$ or $W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(M_{8,1})$ is given.
- Elimination of candidates uses the known low-weight classification and published Euler characteristics; it does not rule out an as-yet-undiscovered non-Tate motive of pure weight $16$ (which would itself be arithmetic news).
- The argument does not prove that the pure piece is Tate—only that known non-Tate sources do not populate it.
- Semisimplicity / comparison between Hodge and Galois realizations is not needed for the elimination above but would be needed for any arithmetic point-count substitute.
assumptions: Standard mixed Hodge theory for smooth Deligne–Mumford stacks and the identification of W_k H^k(M) with the image of restriction from a smooth proper compactification.
Published computations: χ_11(M_{8,1})=0, χ_13(M_{8,1})=-2, and gr^W_13 H_c^{23}(M_{8,1})≅LS_12 (CLPW24/CLPW25b).
Chenevier–Lannes classification used only as a constraint on expected conductor-1 pure motives, not as an unconditional theorem for open moduli beyond what is already proved for k≤15 on \bar M_{g,n}.

claims.statement: For (g,n)=(8,1), d=22, the degree-16 open pure-weight input is exactly W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,1}) ≅ W_{28}H^{28}(M_{8,1})(22), equivalently the pure quotient W_{16}H^{16}(M_{8,1})=im(H^{16}(\bar M_{8,1})→H^{16}(M_{8,1})), expected Tate type Q(8) (BM) / Q(-8) (compact degree 16) / Q(-14) (ordinary untwisted).
gr^W_13 H_c^{23}(M_{8,1}) ≅ LS_12, and by Poincaré duality this pure graded piece pairs with weight 31 in H^{21}(M_{8,1}), not with W_16 H^{16} or W_28 H^{28}.
χ_13(M_{8,1})=-2 (and non-polynomiality of #M_{8,1}(F_q)) does not imply a non-Tate summand of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,1}).

No Tate twist of S_12, LS_12, or S_16 has pure weight 16; Sym^2 S_12 and S_12⊗S_12 first appear only in weight 22; top-weight gr^W_0 is Tate of weight 0. Hence none of these known non-Tate (or top-weight) structures embeds into W_16 H^{16}(M_{8,1}).
Under the Chenevier–Lannes list of conductor-1 motives of weight ≤22, the only pure weight-16 irreducible is Tate; any non-Tate summand of W_16 H^{16}(M_{8,1}) would be arithmetically exceptional.
There is no known geometric construction of a non-Tate direct summand of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,1}), so this search does not refute CONJ-0001 at (8,1).
W_16 H^{16}(M_{8,1}) is itself of Tate type Q(-8) (equivalently the BM target is Q(8)).
H^{16}(\bar M_{8,1};Q) is a direct sum of copies of Q(-8).

gap_markers: GAP-NO-COMPUTATION: No exact calculation of W_16 H^{16}(M_{8,1}) or W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,1}) is supplied.
GAP-NO-COUNTEREXAMPLE: Elimination of known non-Tate sources is not a proof that the pure piece is Tate.
GAP-EXOTIC-MOTIVE: An unknown pure weight-16 non-Tate motive (conductor >1 or outside CL) is not excluded by geometry here.
GAP-CKGP: CKgP / algebraicity methods do not apply in genus 8, so cannot upgrade the search to a positive Tate proof.
GAP-SURVIVAL-ONLY: Even a hypothetical non-Tate class in some mixed graded piece of H^*(M_{8,1}) need not map nontrivially to the pure weight-16 quotient controlling H^{16}(\bar M).
summary: Search for a non-Tate summand in the exact open pure-weight input W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,1}) ≅ W_{28}H^{28}(M_{8,1})(22). Known non-Tate cohomology of M_{8,1} (LS_{12} in weight 13) lives in the wrong bidegree; Chenevier–Lannes conductor-1 motives admit no non-Tate pure weight-16 summand. No surviving counterexample found; pure Tate for this base case remains open.
